title: Nested-array output stability harness with config-delta attribution
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a focused harness to detect quality regressions that specifically impact nested array fields and variable-cardinality structures in model-generated JSON-like outputs when model/config changes are rolled out. Many of our existing structured-output monitors treat objects and flat fields well, but array cardinality, element ordering sensitivity, and optional nested keys are still a common source of silent regressions for customers using list-like responses (e.g., search results, multi-entity extractions, multi-suggestion outputs).

Background / motivation:
- Recent customer incidents and internal postmortems show regressions where top-level schema checks passed but downstream clients broke due to missing array elements or reordered/merged entries.
- Existing field-fidelity signals (presence/shape checks) do not capture subtle losses in element-level consistency, frequency, or multiplicity.
- We need an automated way to tie degradations to a specific model binary, quantization config, or serving config change (model-config delta attribution).

Goals:
1) Create an automated evaluation harness that exercises nested arrays with variable cardinality and reports stability metrics sensitive to omission, duplication, order changes, and per-element attribute drift.
2) Correlate detected instability with model/config deltas (commit sha, model id, quantization profile, runtime flag) to produce suggestive attribution for rollbacks.
3) Integrate with runtime canary/shadow tooling so we can surface these signals before customer-facing rollouts.

Proposed approach:
- Dataset: expand golden anchor set with ~3k examples that include realistic nested-array scenarios (search results, multi-entity extraction, multi-choice enumerations). Add synthetic perturbations (masking optional fields, shuffle-order variants, cardinality augmentation/reduction) to increase coverage.
- Fingerprints: compute array-structure hashes (ordered and unordered variants), per-element anchored-field fingerprints, and an ordered-Jaccard score for element overlap. Store both "soft" similarity metrics and binary contract check results.
- Metrics: implement a composite "Array Stability Index" (ASI) combining:
  * presence_loss_rate (fraction of array entries from anchor missing entirely)
  * duplicate_rate (fraction of arrays with duplicate equivalent entries)
  * order_displacement_score (average normalized Kendall tau for arrays where order matters)
  * element_attr_kl (aggregate KL divergence across numeric attribute distributions inside elements)
  * optional_field_missing_rate (per-field)
- Attribution: when ASI degrades beyond thresholds, run a config-delta tracer that replays the same input batch across the previous stable model/config and the new candidate, capturing token-level diffs, KV-cache effects, and quantization deltas. The tracer produces a ranked list of likely causes: model-architecture-change, quantization-profile, runtime-kernel-switch, or prompt/config change.
- Canary integration: add shadow-eval pipeline that runs ASI on 100% of traffic for 24 hours for any non-trivial rollout (model version bump, quantization change, runtime flag). If ASI regression > 3% absolute or p-value < 0.01 vs baseline, create an automated incident suggestion and annotate the rollout with the failing inputs.

Instrumentation / implementation details:
- New eval module: evals/array_stability_harness.py (unit-tests + integration).
- Offline runner to generate anchors and synthetic variants: scripts/gen_array_anchors.py.
- Storage: store per-example fingerprints and the last-good snapshot in s3://redwood-eval-anchors/array_stability/{model_id}/{commit_sha}/.
- Dashboard: new panel on console-outputs -> Structured Output Integrity called "Array Stability" with per-model, per-config heatmaps and a time series for ASI and each submetric.

Alerting and thresholds:
- Signal severity mapping:
  * P0: ASI regression > 8% absolute or presence_loss_rate > 10% for a critical anchor cohort (customer-facing templates).
  * P1: ASI regression between 3% and 8% or optional_field_missing_rate > 5% across any cohort.
  * P2: smaller signal with rising trend for 3 consecutive windows (24h windows).
- Automated rollback suggestion: generate a ranked list of compatible fallbacks (previous model id, quantization-free variant, lower-seq-length variant) in the incident ticket.

Tradeoffs / alternatives considered:
- Could extend existing schema guards to add array-aware checks, but risk of clutter and high-false-positive rate. Decision: keep array stability harness as a focused eval module that feeds summarized signals into the existing contract monitors.
- Full causal attribution (provable) is expensive; we will produce heuristic-ranked root-cause suggestions and require on-call confirmation before automated rollback.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Harness produces ASI and the five submetrics for all anchors and stores them in the eval metrics DB for query.
- Canary pipeline runs for rollouts and will block promotion when P0 conditions are met.
- Dashboard visualizations are available and linked in the rollout UI.

Release / rollout plan:
1) Prototype: implement offline harness and generate anchors (2 sprints).
2) Integration: wire into shadow-eval runner and push metrics upstream (1 sprint).
3) Visualize & alerting: add dashboard panels and create incident playbook (1 sprint).
4) Gradual enforcement: require ASI check for canaries on all major model or quantization rollouts (rollout policy update).

Related artifacts and links:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/array-stability-harness-proposal
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/core/pull/6123 (WIP)
- Example dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/array-stability-proto

Metrics to track post-launch:
- True-positive rate of ASI alarms vs confirmed regressions (target > 70% first quarter).
- Time to attribution (median) from alert to suggested root cause (< 30 minutes target).
- Fraction of canaries blocked by ASI-based policy (monitor to avoid false positives).
comments: 2025-02-13 - Triage notes: flagged as high-impact after two customer incidents where clients dropped list elements. Assigned to Marcus. Agreed to prioritize anchors that map to public SDK use-cases.

2025-02-20 - Architecture review: decided to compute both ordered and unordered signatures; will include per-field KL and an ordered-Jaccard metric. Design doc updated: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/array-stability-harness-proposal

2025-02-28 - PR opened for prototype anchor generation and fingerprinting (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/core/pull/6123. Unit tests added for unordered hash collisions and basic ASI calculation.

2025-03-03 - QA: initial synthetic batch results show ASI sensitive to quantization changes in one model variant. Replaying inputs across model builds produced signal correlated to a quantization flag change (commit: a1b2c3d). Need to add more anchors for nested depth > 3.

2025-03-05 - Decision log: will not enable automated rollback for first release cycle. Incident suggestions only; on-call must confirm. Dashboard panel ticket created (PM requested visual examples).\n
acceptance_criteria: ASI and submetrics are computed and stored for each anchor within the eval metrics DB
Shadow canary runner can execute ASI on live traffic snapshots and compare to baseline snapshot automatically
Dashboard shows per-model ASI heatmap and time series; rollout UI surfaces latest ASI delta and example failing inputs
Playbook created: instructions for on-call to triage ASI alerts and reproduce with the config-delta tracer
root_cause_hypothesis: Initial QA indicates quantization-profile changes and a runtime kernel switch are the most likely causes for early signals; will verify by replaying inputs across commit shas and quantization profiles using the tracer
rollout_plan: Prototype -> Shadow for one week across non-critical regions -> Add dashboard and alarms -> Require ASI check on canary for major config changes; automated rollback disabled initially
